title: Compact-reservoir KV allocator with sentinel rotation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: continuous batching and long-lived KV entries on GPU lead to micro-fragmentation that degrades effective usable KV capacity and increases per-request memory amplification. Existing slab and segmented allocators do well for steady-state churn but struggle with mixed-lifespan tokens and bursty batch coalescing.

Goal: design and implement a compact-reservoir allocation strategy with a sentinel rotation protocol that reduces fragmentation amplification under live traffic while keeping tail latency stable and preserving fast path allocation/deallocation. Target is >=25% reduction in usable fragmentation (measured as unreachable reserved bytes), <5% increase in 95th-pt latency, and <2% steady-state throughput regression.

Approach summary: build a two-tier allocator composed of (1) compact reservoirs — multiple small contiguous microregions that prefer colocated allocation for tokens with high co-access affinity, and (2) a fast transient pool for short-lived tokens created during large continuous batching windows. Sentinels are lightweight generation tokens embedded into region headers; we rotate sentinels to create compacting epochs that allow lock-free identification and gentle reclamation of dead microregions without global stop-the-world moves. The runtime will record per-region access histograms and affinity hints emitted by the batch scheduler to guide placement and merging.

Why different: unlike previous slab/stripe approaches, this design explicitly coordinates with the continuous batching subsystem to align allocation lifespan hints with microregion placement and uses sentinel rotations to produce inexpensive, parallelizable compaction passes that avoid large GPU kernel synchronizations.

Success criteria and measurable signals are in the acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end test harness shows >=25% reduction in measured unreachable/reserved bytes after 24h of synthetic mixed-lifespan workload compared to baseline allocator.
A2: 95th-pt tail latency increase <=5% on representative L7 test (chat generation with 512-token median sequences) under 80% p99 throughput.
A3: Continuous-batching throughput regression <=2% at default batch size distributions.
A4: No regression in KV hit-rate for prefix caching workloads; telemetry preserved for per-key residency and eviction traces.
A5: New allocator can be toggled via runtime flag and rolled back without requiring model restart or data migration across nodes.
implementation_notes: Use 64-byte sentinel header per microregion containing 8-bit epoch and 24-bit checksum to detect cross-region races.
Affinity hints: extend batch scheduler to annotate tokens with short-lived|medium|long-lived tags (2-bit) emitted in request metadata; these guide pool selection.
Fast path allocation: transient pool uses bump-pointer allocation in persistent allocation buffer with per-thread free lists to keep lock contention minimal.
Compaction pass: sentinel rotation increments epoch; background workers scan microregions in parallel and attempt in-place coalescing if all contained tokens are retired for >=2 epochs.
Memory layout: microregions prefer 16KB alignment to reduce TLB pressure; region headers maintain light-weight free-run lists to avoid linked-list pointer overhead under CUDA constraints.
Fallbacks: when coalescing not possible, mark region as quarantined and proactively replicate high-frequency keys into a new reservoir to avoid cache miss spikes.
Metric hooks: record region_age_histogram, fragmentation_ratio, sentinel_rotation_count, coalesce_success_rate, quarantined_region_count.
blockers: Need kernel-level primitive for atomic region metadata update to avoid races with streamer batching threads (ENG-314159 is related).
GPU firmware bug on 80XX series that increases page migration latency under concurrent compaction passes; platform team tracking fix.
Perf regression in legacy microbench when transient pool falls back to slow free-list path — requires further tuning.
